title: Cybersecurity — Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns Phase Assessment
description: Module checkpoint assessment verifying mastery of learning objectives across: Production Patterns and Resilience in Cybersecurity, Capstone Lab: Verifiable Cybersecurity Implementation.

questions.prompt: [Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns] During a vulnerability scan, a web server responds to requests containing '../../etc/passwd'. What vulnerability does this indicate?
questions.explanation: Path traversal allows attackers to read arbitrary files on the server by stepping up directories using dot-dot-slash patterns.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Production Patterns and Resilience in Cybersecurity

questions.prompt: [Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns] Which defensive measures protect against SQL Injection vulnerabilities?

options.text: Client-side alert boxes warning users not to type quotes

questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate SQL structure from data, completely neutralizing malicious query injection.

questions.prompt: [Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns] What is the primary objective of the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)?

options.text: Every user and service is granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform their legitimate tasks.
All users are assigned administrative privileges to prevent operational bottlenecks.
Password complexity requirements are reduced for internal network users.
Firewalls are configured to allow all outbound traffic unconditionally.

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits blast radius: if an identity is compromised, an attacker cannot pivot beyond that identity's minimal permissions.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Production Patterns and Resilience in Cybersecurity

questions.prompt: [Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns] Why is base64 encoding NOT considered an encryption mechanism?

options.text: Base64 is an encoding scheme with no secret cryptographic key; anyone can decode it instantly without credentials.
Base64 uses 128-bit keys which are easily brute-forced.
Base64 only works on ASCII text.
Base64 is a proprietary hashing algorithm.

questions.explanation: Encoding transforms data representation for transport. Encryption requires secret keys and mathematical algorithms (AES, RSA) to ensure confidentiality.
